subject: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sending a concise proposal for how we’d structure the hosted->dedicated migration so your team has predictable throughput while smoothing cost during the first 6 months. Attached: Redwood-Acme-Transitional-Offer-20270401.pdf (offer summary) and a GPU sizing workbook.

High level (proposal):
- Bridge months: 3 months of reserved bridge capacity (lower commit) to cover expected ramp.
- Conversion credits: $90k conversion credit applied over the first 4 billing cycles (phased: 40% / 30% / 20% / 10%).
- Commit offsets: First-year committed GPU spend backs a 20% discount on per-GPU-hour list pricing vs. standard Dedicated tiers.
- Throughput guarantee: 95th percentile tail latency SLO of 220ms for 1K concurrent chat sessions (L7 model family) or automatic fallback to hosted pool (with 30% higher cost) during sustained overloads.

A few notes/questions for your procurement team before we lock T&Cs:
1) Does Acme need the conversion credit to be invoiced as prepaid credit or an applied bill credit?
2) Any mandated legal terms around audit windows for Reserved capacity billing?
3) Are there any internal PO/contracting timelines we should align to for the bridge months to start (you mentioned an April pilot)?

If this looks directionally right I’ll draft a one-page term sheet and we can route to Legal. Happy to run a short working session to align on GPU sizing in the workbook — Ben is copied and can jump on sizing.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule: calendly.com/redwood/hannah

Attachment: Redwood-Acme-Transitional-Offer-20270401.pdf (6 pages)
Attachment: acme_gpu_sizing_workbook.xlsx (1 sheet)
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <m.torres@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick initial feedback from the product and finance side:
- Bridge months: 3 months is acceptable, but we’d prefer credits to be front-loaded (larger credit in month 1) to offset initial churn during pilot.
- Conversion credits: Can you shift to 60% / 25% / 15% over three cycles instead of 4? Our billing cadence is monthly and we’d like the bulk earlier.
- Commit offsets and discounts look good; procurement will need an estimate of committed GPU hours per month to validate against our internal forecast. I’ll attach our forecast after a quick review.

Also from a legal perspective: we need the throughput guarantee in writing with a clear definition of measurement window (monthly 95th percentile over 5k request samples) and a credits schedule for SLA misses.

Can Ben or Monica run through the sizing workbook with our infra lead tomorrow? Miguel is copied and will coordinate an internal time.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_internal_forecast_v1.csv (referenced)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal

Laura —

Happy to run through the workbook. Proposed plan for tomorrow’s working session:
- 30 min to validate concurrency and p95 targets (we’ll use your 5k sample window).
- 30 min to translate concurrency into average GPU-hours per day and map to Dedicated pool sizes (n1-standard equivalent).
- Quick sketch of two commit profiles: Conservative (smaller commit, higher bridge) and Aggressive (larger commit, higher discount).

Regarding credit pacing: we can accommodate your 60/25/15 on conversion credits — the primary decision point is whether Acme wants the credit as an invoice offset vs. a prepaid balance. Prepaid balance gives you immediate runway but affects your accounting differently. Monica can sync with your procurement on accounting treatment.

Also confirming SLA wording: Redwood will commit to a monthly 95th percentile latency SLO measured over a rolling 30-day window with the sample method you suggested. If we miss the SLO, we’ll provide a service credit equal to 5% of the affected month’s committed spend for each missed month, capped at 20% annually. We’ll put this into the draft term sheet.

I’ll take the action to produce two commit profiles and an updated term sheet draft by Monday.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Miguel Torres <m.torres@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal

Thanks — all. One clarification from infra: if we take the Conservative commit profile, what’s the defined automatic fallback? You noted automatic fallback to hosted pool with ~30% higher unit cost. We need explicit throttling behavior documented (queueing vs reject) and expected cold-start impact on p95.

Procurement also requests: can Redwood add a single bridge month extension option that Acme can exercise within the first 90 days if usage growth lags? Preferable as a one-time opt-in rather than automatic.

I’ll join the sizing session at 11:00 PT today.

—Miguel
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <m.torres@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transitional credit pacing + guaranteed throughput proposal

Miguel —

Good questions. Short answers:
1) Fallback behavior: During sustained overloads that exceed the Dedicated pool + buffer, requests are routed according to policy you pick: a) auto-failover to Redwood hosted pool (best-effort, ~30% higher unit cost, no additional latency SLA), or b) queueing with exponential backoff up to 30s then graceful reject with 429. We recommend auto-failover for production-critical paths; queueing for batch/low-priority workloads.
2) Cold-start impact: fallback to hosted pool may introduce an additional p95 delta of ~60–120ms depending on model size — we’ll measure during the pilot and publish observed deltas in the post-migration report.
3) Bridge extension: yes — we can include a one-time extension clause (30 days) exercisable within the first 90 days. We’ll add language to the draft term sheet and include an example timeline showing how an extension would affect credit pacing.

Action items we’ll take this week:
- Ben: draft Conservative / Aggressive commit profiles + updated pricing table.
- Monica: revise term sheet with SLA credit schedule and bridge extension clause.
- Hannah: upload finalized offer PDF and invite for Wed sizing workshop (calendar invite sent).

Looking forward to tomorrow’s session.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
